note: Family-run private park on US 119 at Putney, between Harlan and Cumberland; despite the name, not a county park. It is the Putney trailhead for the Black Mountain Off-Road Adventure Area and caters to off-road riders (trail shop, pressure wash, welders), with 19 rental cabins beside the RV sites. Sites 1-19 sit in the lower camp by the office; 20-29 are in an upper camp on the hillside with its own shower house. Sites double as electric tent sites. --Claude
summary: Kept with an OHV flag (reviewer). $45 confirmed (dated 2026-11-23, up to 3 people, +$5). 29 electric sites, 50A at most; facilities written; booking via availabilityonline (operator). Google 4.6 (218). Not waterfront confirmed. Pin OK.
flags: OHV (flag only - reviewer decides): the operator markets the park as an off-road base: 'we are the Putney Trailhead for the Black Mountain Off-Road Adventure Area', 'Located directly at Putney Trailhead', Creekside Cabin 'legally ride the shoulder on the same side to the trails', upper camp map 'To Upper Camp, RV Sites 20-30, Upper Shower House & Trails', with a trail shop, pressure wash station, welders and torches. Under the OHV rule (private parks marketing ATV trails starting at the campground are out) this is a DROP CANDIDATE; it also markets itself to construction crews and families ('We welcome groups for local events, construction, or families'), so a reviewer may read it as a general campground with an OHV side.

LONG-STAY: not a long-stay park - all 29 RV sites book by the night online; worker rates are 'depending on availability' by phone. No wording discouraging nightly guests and no minimum stay seen. Nightly share not published.
PRICE: $45 for up to 3 (US$50 gate not triggered).
GOOGLE: 4.6 stars, 218 reviews ('Harlan Co. Campground & Cabins').
SITE COUNT: 19 stored (from note prose) -> 29 (booking list sites 1-29). 50A at sites 1-3, 8, 12-17, 20-21; others amperage unstated (likely 30A).
ACCESS: upper camp (sites 20-29) is reached by a gravel switchback road up the hillside (imagery); the operator states nothing about it, so no action (grades not measured).
WATERFRONT: stored 'not waterfront' confirmed - the camp is on the hillside south of US 119; Poor Fork of the Cumberland River is north of the highway.
